answer: Only water assayed at the spring itself earns a seat, because the assay book holds the mineral content of every spring the survey has visited. A garden bottle filled downstream fails the book: at the pigment of the assay the minerals must match the spring's own water, and river water carries none of them. Forging an assay means bribing a chemist, faking a field trip and paying 8,700, while the sonnet entry in the assay book is read at every bathhouse, so a spring whose water was never tested is turned away.
